solution.homemade: Mix 1 spoon of baking soda, a little vegetable oil, and a small drop of liquid soap in 4 liters of water. Spray every 5–7 days. Remove and burn infected leaves.
solution.chemical: Spray copper-based fungicides like Copper hydroxide or Copper oxychloride. Do not water plants from the top (avoid overhead watering).

solution.homemade: Mix baking soda, vegetable oil, and a few drops of soap in water. Spray on leaves every week. You can also spray neem oil twice a week.
solution.chemical: Use fungicides like Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Difenoconazole to control it.

solution.homemade: Mix one part milk with two parts water and spray every 3 days. Neem oil or garlic spray also helps stop the disease.
solution.chemical: Use fungicides like Metalaxyl, Chlorothalonil, or Mefenoxam. Remove and destroy infected plants quickly.

solution.homemade: Mix 1 spoon baking soda and a little liquid soap in 4 liters of water. Spray once a week. Keep your farm airy and not too wet.
solution.chemical: Spray Chlorothalonil, Copper fungicide, or Azoxystrobin. Clean your greenhouse and don’t plant too close together.

solution.homemade: Crush 10 garlic cloves, soak in 1 liter of water overnight, and spray the next day. Neem oil also helps prevent it.
solution.chemical: Use Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Copper hydroxide fungicide. Remove bad leaves and spray weekly.

solution.homemade: Mix 2 spoons of mild soap in 1 liter of water and spray under the leaves. You can also use neem oil every 3–5 days.
solution.chemical: Use Abamectin, Spiromesifen, or Bifenthrin to kill mites. Change the chemical after some time to stop resistance.

solution.homemade: Mix 1 spoon baking soda and 2 spoons neem oil in 4 liters of water. Spray and cut off lower leaves to allow air to pass.
solution.chemical: Use Mancozeb, Azoxystrobin, or Chlorothalonil every 7–10 days.

solution.homemade: Use neem oil, garlic spray, or yellow sticky traps to control whiteflies that spread this virus. Remove and destroy sick plants.
solution.chemical: Spray insecticides like Imidacloprid, Acetamiprid, or Thiamethoxam to kill whiteflies. Plant tomato types that can resist this virus.

solution.homemade: Mix equal parts milk and water and spray on the leaves. Clean your tools with bleach water (1 part bleach to 9 parts water).
solution.chemical: There is no chemical cure. Use virus-free seeds and resistant tomato varieties. Always clean tools and soil.

solution.homemade: Spray neem oil every week to stop insects. Mix 1 spoon baking soda in 1 liter of water to stop fungus. Use compost tea to make plants strong.
solution.chemical: Use balanced fertilizer (10-10-10) or calcium nitrate to make fruits strong. Spray preventive fungicides or insecticides in the rainy season.
